thread:
emma-cs: FYI customer reported their month-end invoice shows a surprise premium plan line that's not in the dashboard. They say total is $12.3k vs $9.1k in the dashboard. Can we triage?
jon-billing: Account ID? invoice number? any screenshots?
emma-cs: acct: ACCT-8421, invoice #INV-2023-11-582. Screenshot: https://redwood.share/INV-582.png — dashboard shows 90k tokens standard + 10k embeddings but invoice has an extra 200k tokens under 'premium plan' line.
zach-eng: tagging in to look at metering. @jon-billing do we have the raw metering export for that billing window? could be a plan switch boundary or aggregation window overlap.
jon-billing: pulling the metering export now, will attach. Also checking if we applied any manual adjustments/credits.
billing-bot: Invoice generation job ran at 2023-11-01T02:12:07Z. Backfill job for metering-run 2023-10-31 finished at 2023-11-01T01:55:10Z.
jon-billing: attached metering CSV: INV-582-metering.csv (snippet):
```
account,ts,model,tokens,plan
ACCT-8421,2023-10-31T23:58:12Z,text-davinci-003,120000,standard
ACCT-8421,2023-11-01T00:02:05Z,text-davinci-003,80000,premium
ACCT-8421,2023-10-31T23:59:50Z,embed-ada-002,10000,standard
```
emma-cs: hmm there's that 80k premium row right at midnight. Customer says they didn't upgrade until Nov 2.
zach-eng: that looks like a boundary case: metering event at 00:02 UTC but invoice window probably considers 00:00-00:00. If dashboard uses local timezone or a different window it can mismatch. Also notice the 120k standard + 80k premium — maybe a plan-change event caused tokens to be split across plans and invoice grouped differently.
rachel-ops: we had a short delay in plan sync between billing and accounts service on 2023-11-01 00:00:00Z — there was a queued sync that applied plan change retroactively. Could be the sync wrote a plan tag after usage was recorded, making metering attribute to premium for invoice generation.
jon-billing: can you surface the plan-change audit trail? need to know when plan tag was applied to usage rows.
zach-eng: running quick query to aggregate token attribution by ingestion timestamp vs attribution timestamp. Query:
```
SELECT SUM(tokens) AS tokens_by_attr, attribution_plan
FROM metering_usage
WHERE account='ACCT-8421' AND ts >= '2023-10-31' AND ts < '2023-11-02'
GROUP BY attribution_plan;
```
zach-eng: results: standard=130000, premium=80000. But if we group by ingestion_ts bucket (UTC day) we get standard=220000, premium=0. So looks like attribution happened after ingestion.
jon-billing: So invoice used attribution_plan, dashboard uses ingestion window — that explains $ diff. How did attribution change after ingestion?
rachel-ops: plan-change sync writes attribution tags in a backfill process when customer upgrades/downgrades within retention window. In this case sync backfilled 2023-10-31 rows to premium because of a migration script that ran on Nov 1. That backfill was supposed to be opt-in but got enabled globally due to a feature flag flip.
emma-cs: customer insists they were on standard for entire period. They have support portal ticket with screenshots from Oct 31 showing standard plan in app.
zach-eng: we should audit the backfill job run. If it incorrectly reattributed tokens we need to (1) rollback attribution for that account for that window; (2) reissue corrected invoice or credit; (3) patch pipeline to avoid global backfills.
jon-billing: flagged for billing remediation. I'll draft a credit for the extra premium tokens and hold issuing a corrected invoice until we confirm.
rachel-ops: disabling the global backfill flag now. Creating a reproducible run to show the bug: reproduce steps -> run backfill for acct ACCT-8421 with --dry-run to show affected rows.
zach-eng: repro note: the backfill uses 'plan_effective_ts' from accounts table; if plan_effective_ts is null we default to nearest change — that's the bug. Fix is to require explicit plan change event.
emma-cs: I'll notify the customer we'll pause invoice adjustments and that we're investigating, possible credit/workaround.
jon-billing: created ticket BILL-9472 for remediation + accounting review. Adding acct owner @emma-cs to ticket.
billing-bot: CREDIT_CREATED: CR-2023-11-INV582-1 for $3,200 pending approval.
emma-cs: thanks team. Next steps: zach to confirm rollback patch, jon to hold invoice, rachel to patch flag + run scoped backfill, I'll follow up with customer message. :pray:
jon-billing: will update BILL-9472 with timeline by EOD.
zach-eng: I'll open a PR to change backfill behaviour and add a unit test for null plan_effective_ts.
emma-cs: please paste PR link when ready and I'll include it in the customer postmortem.
jon-billing: keeping this thread open until invoice is reconciled.
